item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-2a2ee103120fc0d2","start_unit":12,"end_unit":13,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that it prepared its disability-rights report through consultations with human-rights institutions, civil-society groups, public figures, relevant ministries, national councils, research centers, and task forces, with regular stakeholder meetings and official coordination.","question_ids":["6B.5","8B.5"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The report was submitted in 2020 and describes procedures and institutions operating before or around 2023; it does not establish outcomes specifically during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes these activities to the Government of Egypt; it does not identify Abdel Fattah el-Sisi as personally directing them.","limitations":["Government self-report; independent verification and implementation outcomes are not provided."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2a2ee103120fc0d2","start_unit":18,"end_unit":18,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported economic growth of 5.8 percent and described government policies, oil and gas discoveries, the New Suez Canal, smart-city projects, and presidential initiatives in housing, health, education, youth, women’s empowerment, child and maternal care, and informal settlements.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The figures and examples largely concern years before 2023, including 2019 results; they provide background rather than a 2023-specific outcome.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the policies and presidential initiatives to Egypt’s Government and presidency, but does not identify specific personal decisions by el-Sisi beyond the reference to presidential initiatives.","limitations":["The source is a government submission and gives no independent evaluation, distributional analysis, or full budget execution evidence."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2a2ee103120fc0d2","start_unit":18,"end_unit":18,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported foreign-exchange reserves above $45 billion, unemployment of 7.5 percent in 2019, and inflation of 4.3 percent in September 2019, presenting these as results of government economic plans and policies.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.9","8B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"All quantitative results cited are from 2019 or earlier and therefore do not directly measure the 2023-2023 period.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the results to government economic plans and policies; it does not establish el-Sisi’s personal causal contribution.","limitations":["Historical, government-reported indicators; no 2023 data or independent causal assessment is supplied."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2a2ee103120fc0d2","start_unit":19,"end_unit":19,"fact_summary":"Egypt’s constitutional framework assigns the president head-of-state and executive authority, commander-in-chief status, a six-year term, and a maximum of two consecutive presidential terms; the president and cabinet jointly set and oversee general state policy.","question_ids":["4B.2","4B.8","8B.2"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"The report describes the constitutional framework in force during the reporting period, relevant as institutional context for 2023.","ruler_attribution":"These are formal constitutional powers and limits applicable to el-Sisi as president; the extract does not document his compliance or non-compliance in 2023.","limitations":["Formal rules alone do not establish actual contestability, enforcement, or restraint."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2a2ee103120fc0d2","start_unit":19,"end_unit":19,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that the president tasks the prime minister with forming the government and presenting its programme to the House of Representatives; if the government lacks majority confidence, the president instructs the prime minister to nominate the majority party or coalition to form a government.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.4","8B.2","8B.5"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"The extract describes constitutional arrangements relevant to 2023 but does not document a 2023 confidence event or government-formation decision.","ruler_attribution":"The powers are attributed to the presidency under the Constitution, not to a specific 2023 act by el-Sisi.","limitations":["No evidence is supplied about actual legislative independence, coalition bargaining, or acceptance of opposition outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2a2ee103120fc0d2","start_unit":19,"end_unit":19,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that local administrative units have legal personality and independent budgets, that local councils are directly elected for four-year terms, and that seats are reserved for youth, women, workers and farmers, Christians, and persons with disabilities; councils may oversee executive authorities and cannot be dissolved through a general administrative procedure.","question_ids":["4B.4","4B.7","8B.2","8B.5"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"These are constitutional and statutory arrangements described for the reporting period; the extract does not show whether local elections or councils operated in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The provisions are attributed to Egypt’s constitutional system, not to a documented personal initiative of el-Sisi.","limitations":["The source does not establish implementation, actual local-government autonomy, or enforcement of reserved representation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2a2ee103120fc0d2","start_unit":19,"end_unit":19,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that the judiciary is independent, judges cannot be dismissed and are answerable only to law, and the Supreme Constitutional Court has an independent budget whose published judgments are binding on all state authorities.","question_ids":["3B.4","4B.4","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The claim concerns the legal framework in force before and during 2023, but does not document actual judicial decisions or independence during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes these safeguards to the constitutional order rather than to an individual act by el-Sisi.","limitations":["Government description of formal guarantees; no evidence here tests political interference or compliance with adverse judgments."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2a2ee103120fc0d2","start_unit":20,"end_unit":20,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported constitutional guarantees of human dignity, a prohibition on torture without a statute of limitations, equality and non-discrimination, and protection of personal freedom from arrest, search, detention, or restriction except pursuant to a substantiated judicial order required for an investigation.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","4B.3","4B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"These are formal constitutional guarantees relevant during 2023; the extract does not show actual enforcement or remedy during that year.","ruler_attribution":"The guarantees are attributed to the Constitution and state institutions, not to a specific el-Sisi decision.","limitations":["Formal legal protections do not establish compliance in practice."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2a2ee103120fc0d2","start_unit":22,"end_unit":22,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported constitutional protections for press, print, audiovisual, and digital-media freedom; peaceful assembly and protest after legal notification; formation of political parties; and formation of civil associations through notification.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.6","4B.8"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The report describes constitutional rules relevant to 2023 but does not document their practical application in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The provisions are attributed to the constitutional framework and not to a documented personal act by el-Sisi.","limitations":["The extract does not address restrictions, enforcement practices, or remedy for violations."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2a2ee103120fc0d2","start_unit":24,"end_unit":24,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that the National Council for Human Rights may report violations to the Public Prosecutor, intervene in civil proceedings at an injured party’s request, and that laws regulating elections, political parties, the judiciary, and constitutional rights require a two-thirds House majority.","question_ids":["3B.4","4B.1","4B.4","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"These legal mechanisms were described as in force before 2023; no 2023 case or intervention is identified.","ruler_attribution":"The mechanisms are attributed to Egyptian law and institutions, not to an individual 2023 action by el-Sisi.","limitations":["The source does not establish that the council or supermajority requirement effectively constrained executive power."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2a2ee103120fc0d2","start_unit":24,"end_unit":24,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that independent national human-rights mechanisms have legal personality and technical, financial, and administrative independence, may report violations, monitor treaty implementation, visit prisons and detention facilities, and intervene in judicial cases on behalf of victims.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.6","7B.6","7B.7","8B.5"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The mechanisms are described as existing before 2023; the extract does not provide 2023 activity or findings.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes these powers to the Constitution and enabling laws, without documenting el-Sisi’s personal use or protection of them.","limitations":["Government self-description; practical independence, access, and follow-through are not independently demonstrated."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2a2ee103120fc0d2","start_unit":39,"end_unit":39,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that the House Human Rights Committee has authority and tools to monitor government and executive performance, including field visits and participation in drafting relevant laws.","question_ids":["3B.4","4B.4","7B.6","8B.5"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The committee’s described powers predate 2023; no 2023 monitoring result is supplied.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the authority to the House of Representatives, not to el-Sisi personally.","limitations":["No evidence is provided about whether the committee could act independently or whether its findings produced correction."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2a2ee103120fc0d2","start_unit":39,"end_unit":39,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that a Supreme Permanent Committee for Human Rights was established by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 2396 of 2018 to follow up implementation of international and regional obligations, propose legislative measures, develop awareness and capacity programmes, and cooperate with international and regional bodies.","question_ids":["3B.4","6B.9","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The committee was established in 2018; the extract does not document its 2023 outputs or effectiveness.","ruler_attribution":"The institution is attributed to a prime-ministerial decree and government structure; el-Sisi’s personal role is not specified.","limitations":["No independent assessment of staffing, resources, autonomy, or implementation is included."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2a2ee103120fc0d2","start_unit":40,"end_unit":40,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that the National Council for Childhood and Motherhood has legal personality and an independent budget, oversees a Child and Maternal Welfare Fund, proposes national policy and plans, monitors implementation, evaluates reports, and issues directives to remove obstacles.","question_ids":["6B.3","6B.4","6B.5","6B.9","8B.2","8B.5","8B.8"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The institutional arrangements predate 2023 and are not accompanied by 2023 implementation or outcome data.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes these functions to the council and statutory framework, not to a specific act by el-Sisi.","limitations":["Formal mandates and reported functions do not establish actual funding, coverage, or corrective impact."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2a2ee103120fc0d2","start_unit":40,"end_unit":40,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that the National Council for Women has financial and administrative independence and is responsible for promoting women’s rights, monitoring national plans, proposing policy, coordinating with ministries and NGOs, and addressing discrimination.","question_ids":["3B.7","4B.7","6B.3","6B.8","6B.9","8B.2","8B.5"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The council’s legal framework predates 2023; no 2023 implementation or outcome evidence is supplied.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes these functions to the council and Act No. 30 of 2018, not to a documented personal decision by el-Sisi.","limitations":["No independent evidence of actual reach, resources, or reduction in discrimination is provided."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2a2ee103120fc0d2","start_unit":41,"end_unit":41,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that the National Council for Human Rights has technical, financial, and administrative independence, may review complaints and alleged violations, visit prisons and detention facilities, report violations to the Public Prosecutor, and support victims in judicial cases.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The council’s legal powers were described as existing before 2023; no 2023 complaint, visit, referral, or remedy is identified.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the powers to Act No. 94 of 2003 as amended in 2017 and the constitutional framework, not to a specific el-Sisi action.","limitations":["The source does not establish actual independence, access, investigative findings, or government compliance."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2a2ee103120fc0d2","start_unit":41,"end_unit":41,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that Act No. 149 of 2019 permits civil associations to be established by notification absent administrative objection, treats non-objection within 60 working days as approval, bars administrative dissolution without a judicial ruling, and provides access to funding, grants, and support funds.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.9","6B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The law was promulgated in 2019 and was part of the framework relevant to 2023; the extract does not show actual administration or enforcement in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the rules to Act No. 149 of 2019; it does not document el-Sisi’s personal implementation or intervention.","limitations":["The account is government-reported and does not address administrative practice, funding restrictions, or enforcement against associations."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2a2ee103120fc0d2","start_unit":42,"end_unit":43,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that Act No. 10 of 2018 and related measures created disability-rights definitions, duties, reasonable-accommodation requirements, accessibility standards, and coordination mechanisms; the Government declared 2018 the Year of Persons with Disabilities and continued coordination with state institutions and NGOs.","question_ids":["3B.7","4B.7","6B.2","6B.3","6B.8","6B.9","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The principal measures were adopted in 2018 and described in a 2020 report; they provide institutional background but not 2023 outcomes.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the measures to the Egyptian Government, Constitution, Act No. 10 of 2018, and implementing regulations; it does not isolate el-Sisi’s personal direction.","limitations":["No independent evidence of accessibility, service uptake, employment, or equal-rights outcomes is provided."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The supplied document is a government response/report concerning disability rights and constitutional arrangements, with most evidence predating 2023; it contains no direct account of Abdel Fattah el-Sisi’s personal conduct, no independent adverse findings, and little period-specific outcome evidence.","The extracted HTML includes encoding artifacts, but the cited units contain sufficiently legible substantive text for the records above."]}
